agree.reason: For a retiree who uses or values the Ridgeview branch, the July closure and a concrete $10 a month on their own home could move them, but the script never says what is different from the levy they voted against, so a firm No probably stays No.

honest.reason: Every figure checks out ($640k × 0.19 = $121.60 a year, about $10.13 a month, about $2.34 a week), and the writer rightly dropped the 'less than a coffee a month' claim, but 'more than ever' goes beyond a 22% rise since 2021, and 'this one will be close too' is a guess.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out yearly, monthly, weekly and per-home costs from the rate, uses the Ridgeview median rather than the city one, and gives a do-it-yourself formula, though a per-day figure or the citywide $78-a-year figure was left unused.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated as the facts show it: the Ridgeview branch closes in July and Sunday hours stay gone, set against rising use, the 22% increase in visits.

qualification.reason: The July closure is a dated consequence the reader can check, but 'this one will be close too' cannot be checked, and the exemption line is an unfilled placeholder.

objections.reason: It answers the 'blank check' charge directly with the fixed rate, the six-year limit and the named uses, and it addresses fixed income with a real number, but it doesn't say why this levy deserves a vote that the last one didn't.

fit.reason: The main pitch runs about 60 to 90 seconds and the layout suits a card, though the objection section may make it tight to fit on one side.
